title: Assignment web design roofer company
description: Assignment web designWEbdWhen designing a website for a roofer in the Netherlands, it is essential to clearly explain what a roofer's tasks entail. A roofer is a specialist focused on the protection and maintenance of roofs. Their work is crucial for ensuring the durability and safety of buildings. The services offered by a roofer cover a wide range of specializations, including repairing roof tiles, ridge tiles, and chimneys, as well as maintenance and installation of zinc work. They are also skilled in detecting and repairing roof leaks, repairing storm damage, and working with various types of roofing materials such as bitumen roofs and slate roofs.Another important service is cleaning and insulating roofs. Regularly cleaning a roof can significantly extend its lifespan and improve the aesthetic value of the building. Roof insulation is also an essential service, as properly insulated roofs contribute to significant energy savings and improved comfort within the building.Delivering quality and ensuring customer satisfaction are central to the philosophy of a professional roofer. It is crucial to choose a specialist with a lot of experience, as the roof is one of the most important parts of a building. An experienced roofer can not only provide the best solutions but also advise on preventive maintenance to avoid future problems.Roofers often operate within specific regions or areas, allowing them to quickly respond to their customers' needs and provide personalized, tailor-made services. Therefore, when choosing a roofer, it is advisable to select a professional familiar with the specific challenges and climate conditions of your region.Conversion and SEOA website for a roofer should clearly highlight these aspects, emphasizing the expertise, services offered, and the importance of choosing an experienced specialist to ensure the durability and safety of your roof.For an effective website for a roofing company, it's essential that it is not only informative and user-friendly but also SEO-optimized and conversion-oriented. This means that the website should be designed to rank high in the search results of search engines like Google, on relevant keywords that potential customers might use when looking for roofing services. A good SEO strategy includes the use of relevant keywords, optimizing website speed, mobile friendliness, and creating quality content that meets the needs of the target audience.Additionally, the website must be conversion-oriented. This means that the design and structure of the website are focused on encouraging the visitor to take action, in this case, to contact the roofing company. This can be achieved by placing clear call-to-action (CTA) buttons at strategic locations on the website, such as 'Request a quote', 'Contact us for a free inspection', or 'Call us now'. Ensure that contact information is clearly visible on every page of the website, and consider using contact forms that are easy and quick to fill out.Therefore, the goal of the website is not only to inform visitors about the services and specializations of the roofing company, such as repairs of roof tiles, ridge tiles, chimneys, zinc work, roof leaks, storm damage, bitumen roofs, slate roofs, roof cleaning, and roof insulation, but also to motivate them to take action. By making the website SEO-optimized and conversion-oriented, you increase the chance that potential clients will find the roofing company and get in touch, which ultimately can lead to more assignments and growth of the business.Principles:- Style guide (see attachment)- Example website https://www.walterdakwerken.nl/, the pages of the new site should contain the same elements and functionality. title: Javascript- Graphics and Animation
description: Part IOverview:In the first part of the final project, you will set up a complex scene by loading from two simple file formats—OBJ models accompanied by MTL material files. You will then apply lighting and texturing. When it is done, your scene will consist of a lit and colored car sitting on a lit and colored road next to a lit and textured stop sign, illuminated by a lit and colored streetlamp.Part 1-1: Setting your SceneThe first step is to review the starter code for this project. It contains a Model and a Face class and a series of calls that take in OBJ and MTL files and parses them into Model objects. Make sure you understand what this code is doing and what it returns so that you know how to use it in your program. You are welcome (but not required) to make any modifications to this code that you see fit. If you see any errors in this starter code or have any suggestions for improvement, let the instructor know.The starter code produces several console.log() statements that allow you to look at everything that has been processed from the files. You should study these statements to understand how the data in the Model class is organized. In particular, node how Model has an array of Face instances that contain all of the vertices, normals, and texture coordinates for each face in that model. The faces have all been triangulated for you, so you can just pass them directly into the vertex shader (either one face at a time or all at once) to draw your mesh using gl.TRIANGLES. Each face also has a corresponding material field that references one of the materials in the diffuseMap and specularMap fields in Model. You can use this information to look up the appropriate values for your lighting calculations on that face.Once you are comfortable with the above information, you should then render your models in a simple view to verify that your program is working. (HINT: Start with the stop sign, since it's the simplest mesh.) You will then want to set up your scene as shown in the demo video (you will incorporate the bunny in a later step). Once everything is set up correctly, you should then turn your attention to the MTL files.Diffuse colors in the form “Kd [R] [G] [B]”Specular colors in the form “Ks [R] [G] [B]”A diffuse texture map in the form “map_Kd [Map Image]”Part 1-2: LightingNext, you will place a point light at the top of your streetlamp to illuminate your scene. Your light should use Phong shading, and you should use the previously loaded diffuse and specular material colors from the MTL file. You may create your own ambient color.Allow the user to press the ‘L’ key to toggle the light on/off, but make sure that ambient light is still applied to your scene even when the light is off.Implementation Notes:Your lighting will likely look flat simply due to the normals on the provided models not being smoothed.Part 1-3: TexturingNext, you will implement texturing in your program using the texture coordinates loaded from the stop sign’s OBJ file, accompanied by the stop.png texture as specified in the map_Kd attribute of the material in stopsign.mtl.Implementation Notes:The texture coordinates in the OBJ file are flipped along the Y-axis; to get your final texture coordinates, you should subtract the V coordinates from 1.Part 1-4: Camera AnimationFinally, you will implement basic camera animation so that the user can view your scene from different angles. When the user presses the ‘C’ key, make the camera move along a circle on the XZ plane, while bobbing up and down slightly (along the Y-axis) as shown in the demo. (HINT: Think about how you might use the trigonometric functions.) The camera should not jump at all when the user starts or stops the animation and should preserve its current state.Part IIFinal Project Part II DemoLinks in starter fileOverview:In the second part of the final project, you will use a matrix stack to structure your scene through hierarchical transformations. You will also implement simple shadows, reflections, and refractions.Part 2-1: Hierarchical TransformationsPart 2-2: Hierarchical CameraPart 2-3: ShadowsPart 2-4: SkyboxPart 2-5: Reflections and Refractions (i.e. Environment Maps)Make bids and I will share more details and files also in chats.Happy Bidding!!!

This individual will also play a pivotal role in conducting thorough market research and analysis to inform our strategic marketing decisions across our platforms.Marketing Assistant Responsibilities:1. Manage and grow social media accounts for our boat charter business, vacation rentals, and remodeling company, including Instagram, Facebook, Twitter, and Pinterest.2. Trend Identification: Stay abreast of industry trends, consumer preferences, and emerging technologies in the boating, hospitality, and real estate markets. Proven experience in social media management, content creation, and online advertising, preferably in the travel, hospitality, or construction industries.2. Strong writing and editing skills with a keen eye for detail and creativity to produce compelling and engaging marketing materials.3. Proficiency in using social media management tools, email marketing platforms, and analytics tools to track and measure performance metrics.4. Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate effectively with team members, clients, and external partners in a remote work environment.5. Self-motivated and proactive with the ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines independently while maintaining a high level of accuracy and quality.6. Knowledge of SEO principles, website optimization, and digital marketing strategies to enhance online visibility and drive organic traffic.7. Familiarity with boating, vacation rentals, or remodeling industries is a plus but not required.8. Bachelor's degree in marketing or related field is preferred.

title: Seeking ChatGPT or LLM specialist to write a bunch of articles
description: Hi,I am seeking a ChatGPT or just about any LLM specialist to craft AI-generated articles on a list of keywords that I give you. I currently have a list of about 32 keywords that I am trying to target and I need you to use your preferred tool of choice to write a [PHONE] word entry for each of them. You need to instruct your tool of choice to write the articles in a way that mentions the target keyword as much as possible without compromising on the readability of the article.At the beginning and end of the article, it should also mention the company name that provides the service the article is about and link to its site. All in all, it's a very straightforward process, just automating the writing of content marketing articles. I was doing it myself but it's getting too cumbersome submitting several prompts to ChatGPT 4.0 for each article (as it can't write 2000-3000 word articles in one-go, you have to break them into separate sections and them combine them afterwards).Please also make sure that the articles aren't written too generically. You want part of your prompt engineering to include the act of instructing it to write in a more human manner that will relate to the readers, otherwise it'll just end up writing the articles in a way that is now easily detectable as AI-generated content by most people.I've found that finding content relevant to the keyword online and copy-and-pasting/feeding it the information from those articles makes it so it doesn't give you the most generic information imaginable. You just tell it to then re-write it in a fashion that sounds more human and it will do a relatively good job of that. Then just have it insert the company in one of the paragraphs in the introduction and conclusion. The introduction needs to be subtle and relevant, I do not want the articles coming off as too "salesy".I am looking to pay $3 per finished article and will have probably another couple hundred keywords that I'll need to target in the near future. Assuming you can churn out a finished article every 10-15 minutes like I was doing, this job will be paying about $12-$18 an hour. Send your proposals my way if you are interested.

title: Figma to Wordpress with Open AI integration
description: We have a simple Figma design for a small webapp that is to be integrated into an existing wordpress page and integrated with our Open AI API. You can view the Figma here:https://www.figma.com/file/zRfiP3zA62LF93ZUEpK70i/ME-KIBA?type=design&node-id=0%3A1&mode=design&t=Xg6x9SmBgeYUKZbE-1What the web app does: The web app as visualized in Figma is meant as a landing page for business partners who agreed to review a service that has been provided to them. They will be offered assistance in writing their review via an AI-Text-Assistant (AITA). If they opt for the assistant, they will be asked which areas of the service provided they liked best and want to see mentioned in the review. These can be selected. Then the AITA will compose the review (via Open AI API) and present the result on the next page. This result can be copied to the clipboard by the user, so it can be used when placing the actual review on Google or Proven Experts (a review portal).The Figma: The design in figma was done in a simple manner. No components have been defined, no Auto-Layout, etc. However, the web app is very simple and consits only of four pages / steps.Responsiveness: The current design is meant for a mobile view and we would like to stick to that design in desktop and tablet view by making it appear like a form. Example:https://s38924.pcdn.co/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/ftl-contact-form.jpgOn the smartphone, the header and footer of the wordpress page will need to be hidden from view, so that only the web app becomes visible.On desktop and tablet, the web app will appear like a form of the wordpress page.The Open AI integration: We already have a successful integration in place via Gravity Forms and their Open AI plugin. This could be used if you can make it work with the design.If you chose to use the existing Gravity Forms integration, the main challenge seems to get the result from the Open AI query to show up in our properly designed "page 3" instead of the Gravity Forms notification page (this is how it works out of the box after clicking submit).If you do not want to use Gravity Forms, we could run our own python script (which we would provide you) or use a different plugin.Page 2 functionality: We will need to be able to add or remove the selectable options in the Wordpress backend. We may want to add "Great customer support" some time in the future or remove an option. The selectable boxes must either be flexibly arrange themselves a) in the lenght of each box according to text displayed and b) to minimize white space between boxes. Alternatively, we can also live with a different design option as long as it looks good.Page 3 functionality: In the Figma, the result shows in a scrollable text box. The user should be able to edit the text here, if he likes. The button "Copy to Clipboard" should do just that.General:- The web app should work on most of todays devices and browsers.- The "form entries" should be collected with the review generated AND with the review that was present when the user clicks "Next". This way we can analyze if the user modified the proposed text.Timeline: We would like to complete this project as soon as possible, preferably until the 23rd of February at the latest.Please do not send AI-generated project proposals :)Thank you and I am looking forward to e-meeting you.

title: WordPress Plugin Development for Backlinks
description: Looking to develop a Backlink Network plugin.When installed, it will create a dashboard for the user. The dashboard will contain a number of tabs.1. 1st tab will display a list of all pages/posts on the WordPress site. It will contain Page Title, Keyword Focus from Yoast and URL. It will also show how many backlinks have been added to this URL from the backlink network.2. 2nd tab will contain Inventory of Pages/Posts in the Network inventory.3. Each WordPress site will gain backlink credits. When installed they will receive 2 free credits. This will be displayed at the top of the dashboard.4. The website owner will review the Network Inventory and select a keyword + URL, then manually add to a page/post. Once added, they will return to the inventory + submit for review by providing the URL where the link was added.5. The plugin will verify the link exists and then send backlink details (URL + keyword) to Network Inventory.6. The network inventory database will have a backlink record for each URL and then update the backlink count on the inventory.7. When a site receives a backlink the dashboard will display a backlink count on the Site Page/Post in the 1st tab above.8. For every 2 backlinks added, the website will earn 1 backlink credit to be used in the 1st tab above.9. From the 1st tab, the user will select Pages/Posts to be displayed in the network inventory based on the number of backlink credits available. To start each user will receive 2 free credits. Each time they add 2 backlinks they will earn 1 more credit.10. A user can remove backlinks from their site, this will adjust their link credits and auto adjust which posts/pages display in the network inventory. This should be rescanned daily.11. If a user does not want to earn backlink credits, they can purchase.12. User can change which Pages/Posts they wish to include in the inventory at any time by selecting/unselecting from 1st tab even if they have received backlinks.13. To earn credits, a maximum of 3 backlinks will be allowed per URL. When scanning URL for backlinks to verify credits it should be based on a date the backlink was added. Therefore oldest backlinks should be counted 1st, any new links will not be counted after 3/URL.14. Backlinks added will required rel=dofollow to be counted for credit. When re-scanning backlinks daily, it should monitor for valid parameters.Will need the plugin maintained over time and help submitting to WordPress plugin directory. The initial plugin will not offer option to buy credits, we will add this in the future.

title: Node.js sandbox
description: Hi there -I'm looking for a javascript pro to put together a bare-bones node.js express app that gives the user a code sandbox using StackBlitz WebContainers.You can read more about WebContainers here:https://webcontainers.io/guides/introductionIt is a browser based runtime that allows the running of a node application in the browser (all local).Basically, this is a project to set up their hello-world example, but using plain javascript (not Vite), and with one extra feature (file upload)What is a code sandbox? It's:1. Code entry: A textarea where the user can write code2. Output: An output window where the results of the code run are shown (error or successful output)3. File upload: A file upload button that allows the user to upload files to the sandbox, so that they're accessible to the code that was pasted into the code-entry boxI'm attaching a wireframe so that you can see how it works.There's not much that's complicated here - just following the StackBlitz tutorial.The deliverable is:- A node express app that displays the sandbox UI- A route that uploads files to the WebContainer- A route that runs code Posted by the user, which includes- Installing npm libs specified in the user's code- A method for the user to access files that were uploaded in their code snippet (just a path convention)- Outputs the results to the output boxThat's it. Should be fun! WebContainers are awesome.

title: Dev for business process automations
description: I'm looking for a dev with the following skills:Automation of business processesGoogle SheetsWordpressIntegrationsZapier/Web hooksPayment processors like StripeAPIHere’s an example of a process I'd like to create:Imagine your car broke down. You used the online store to order and pay for a tow. You chose Stripe as the payment processor. It accepted your $500 deposit and put it on "hold". The tow truck arrived and towed you to your garage. The tow truck driver submitted his final mileage/gas/time totalling $200 to the tow truck company. The tow truck company adds their $100 service fee to make a total of $300. They submit $300 as the capture amount to Stripe and receive it in their account. The tow truck company sends the driver $150 (the company keeps $50 as a service fee) and so they make $150. The remaining $200 is released back to your card as available funds. That completes it.How do they do the deposit part? It's described in Stripe's documentation here:https://stripe.com/docs/payments/place-a-hold-on-a-payment-methodIf you prefer Paypal's documentation:https://developer.paypal.com/docs/checkout/standard/customize/authorization/The request needs to come from somewhere. It could be a form like WPforms. It could be out of the box from woocommerce. There likely needs to be integration with plugins like Quickbooks or Expensify. The data needs to be stored somewhere like Google Sheets. It also requires a booking plugin integration with something like WPamelia or another with a round robin feature. We might need a hidden strand to assign to the order.If you're familiar with what I've described you're likely a good fit.This isn't about site design or layout. I'm using Divi to build the site myself. I'm happy to work with someone who wants to consult through the process and/or step in where necessary.Thank you for your consideration.

title: Data Analysis for Human Activity Recognition Thesis
description: Thank you for your willingness to assist with my project. To ensure you're off to a solid start, I wanted to clarify a few points.I'm currently finalizing my Bachelor's thesis, having completed a thorough introduction and literature review, which I'll share in an attached file. You're not required to read it in full, but here's a summary of the literature review's conclusion: The integration of wearable and ambient sensors in Human Activity Recognition (HAR) shows promise, yet the full potential of their combined use remains largely untapped. The existing research underscores the unique contributions of both sensor types to HAR, suggesting a more comprehensive approach could significantly enhance system accuracy and applicability. – My research question is: How does the performance of HAR methods vary when utilizing data from wearable sensors compared to stationary environmental sensors, and how can these methods be integrated to enhance one another?Your task involves analyzing the OPPURTINITY dataset featuring both ambient and wearable sensors, with the aim of determining how they can be synergistically used for activity detection. Start by evaluating the wearable sensors' accuracy independently, then assess the impact of integrating both types of sensors on accuracy. This analysis will inform our understanding of how to merge these sensors for superior HAR performance. The dataset is labeled with specific activities, allowing for precise accuracy measurements of the HAR system.Please read the dataset description very closely here: https://archive.ics.uci.edu/dataset/226/opportunity+activity+recognitionFeel free to utilize models from existing research, and please avoid designing new models yourself. This will take way too much time. Here are some resources you might find useful:- https://github.com/yashbhagat3/Human-Activity-Recognition-using-LSTMs-Opportunity-UCI-Dataset-- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s[PHONE]- https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/jindongwang92/crossposition-activity-recognitionEnsure all references are correctly cited, and aim for simplicity in your analysis. I'll also send you some example theses for format guidance. It should be concise and to the point.I've included a file from a previous attempt at this analysis for your reference. While it didn't align with my expectations, there might be aspects of it you could find useful. I'm interested in your thoughts on this prior work. Specifically, it lacked precision; it offered a general overview rather than detailing the specific approach he was going to take. For example, rather than a broad statement like:"Low-pass filtering techniques are commonly applied to the raw sensor data to remove high-frequency noise while preserving essential signals related to human movement."I'm looking for a more direct explanation, such as:" Method X has been applied to process the sensor data..."Additionally, the content needs to be more focused. His attempt included too much information irrelevant to the methodology section, which would have been better suited for the introduction or literature review (which I had already made). Please ensure your analysis succinct and relevant, clearly outlining how you conducted it without unnecessary elaboration.I have attached a file of an example thesis. The example thesis provided is for reference on the writing style of the methodology and results sections, even though it covers a different topic. This is the kind of format and approach I envision for my own thesis eventually.I'd like you to concentrate specifically on the data analysis. After completing your analysis, please provide a detailed account of the methods you employed.Given the time already been wasted, a fast completion would be greatly appreciated and rewarded! Thank you so much for your help.If your interested in this job, please send me a plan on how you are going to tackle this, specifically.

title: Evaluating the Quality of Machine-generated Explanations
description: IntroductionAuthor attribution is the task of identifying the author of a given text based on the writing style. In this study, you will evaluate the quality of explanations generated by machine learning models that justify their decision on specific tasks of author attribution. The task consists of two phases: Phase 1 and Phase 2. In the following, we will explain each.Note: Because a portion of the data comes from social media posts, it is possible that you come across potentially distressing content or ideas. However, this content might not be extreme and can be found in public social media. By accepting to perform this task, you agree to participate in this study; you have the right to stop annotating at any time.In both phases, you will solve 70 tasks, each taking between 15 and 20 minutes.Phase 1:This phase consists of solving two types of tasks that we explain below (Task 1 and Task 2). You will be solving 50 tasks in total; each task is expected to take a maximum of 20 minutes to complete.Task 1:Task context. Law enforcement has identified a forum post we call a Query document (Q document). An investigation has resolved the origin of the post to a particular device such that it must have been written by one of the four potential authors: A, B, C, or D. Law enforcement need to know if there is evidence to support identifying one of the suspects for further investigation.Task description. Your task is to read the Query document as well as the posts from each author and determine which of the candidate authors is likely to have written the Query documents. In some of these tasks, you will also be given extra explanations of the linguistic, stylistic, and/or semantic features of the Query document, as well as posts from each author.Then, only if this information is given, you will have to answer a set of questions on the quality of explanations.Task 2:Task context. Same as Task 1 contextTask description. This time, you will be presented with an AI agent’s prediction of the Query document's author and the machine-generated explanation that justifies this prediction. Your task is to judge different aspects of the explanation you just saw with respect to the prediction.Annotation PlatformOn the annotation platform, click on the “Author Attribution Explanation” project. You will then be prompted with a summary of the instructions, and then you can start the evaluation. The total 50 tasks are composed of 10 sets of 5 tasks each, sequentially presented to you. Each set consists of the same Query and Author documents. The first task in the set consists of you solving the Type 1 task without any provided explanations. The second and third tasks in the set consist of you solving the Type 1 task but with explanations provided by two systems (describing the documents’ writing style and the overall similarity). The fourth and fifth tasks are of Type 2, where we additionally show the AI agent prediction by the two systems, and you have to answer questions regarding the prediction.Noe: More details on this Phase can be found in the Phase 1 Study Instruction and Info Sheet in the attachments.Phase 2:For each task, you will be presented with a query document and four candidate documents, along with the AI’s prediction of the author of the query document with explanations of the decision. Then, you will reason about the AI’s prediction on a follow-up document. You are to guess what the AI would predict. In total, you will solve 20 tasks.Note that your task is NOT to annotate the correct answers to the follow-up questions but rather guess the Robot's answers based on its explanation and answer in the starter text.

title: Optimization and Deployment of AI News Analysis Web App
description: IntroductionWe have developed an AI News Analysis web app that leverages Python for its development. The application integrates Bing News and Search API, as well as the OpenAI API, to enhance user input queries. The primary objective of this web application is to provide users with immediate answers to their queries through news and web search. The application consists of three main components, all of which utilize both the OpenAI and Bing APIs.Current challenges:Our current challenge is that the application code is not optimized, contains many unused libraries,and the code not the best which results in a larger Docker image. This issue hinders our ability to deploy our API on AWS Lambda functions.ObjectiveThe main goal is to rewrite the application code from scratch for optimization & enhancement, develop an API for the existing functions using FastAPI, and deploy the optimized application on AWS Lambda functions. This will ensure that the application is efficient, scalable, and meets the deployment requirements of AWS Lambda.Scope of Work1. Code Analysis• Objective: Study and understand the current codebase to extract the necessary logic and functionalities.• Tasks:• Review the existing web app's codebase.• Identify key functionalities, algorithms, and logic used in the application.• Document the core components and their interactions.2. Code Rewrite• Objective: Rewrite the application code from scratch using the documented logic and functionalities as a reference, ensuring optimization and efficiency.• Tasks:• Develop a clean, optimized codebase using Python, focusing on minimizing dependencies and removing unused libraries.• Ensure the new codebase adheres to best practices for scalability, maintainability, and performance.• Incorporate Bing News and Search API and OpenAI API integrations as per the existing logic.3. FastAPI Development• Objective: Develop a FastAPI-based API for all the application functions to facilitate easy integration and scalability.• Tasks:• Design and implement API endpoints for each functionality of the web app.• Ensure comprehensive API documentation for ease of use and integration.• Implement authentication and authorization mechanisms to secure API access.4. Deployment on AWS Lambda• Objective: Deploy the optimized application on AWS Lambda functions, ensuring that the deployment is efficient and the application is scalable.• Tasks:• Containerize the FastAPI application using Docker, ensuring the Docker image is optimized for size and performance.• Set up the AWS Lambda environment and configure it to host the Docker container.• Implement CI/CD pipelines for automated testing and deployment of the application.Deliverables• A fully rewritten and optimized codebase for the AI News Analysis web app.• A fully functional FastAPI API for the web app's functionalities.• Documentation covering the API endpoints, usage, and integration guide.• A deployed and functional version of the application on AWS Lambda.Project TimelineThe project is expected to be completed within TWO WEEKS, from the commencement date. A detailed timeline will be provided upon project initiation, outlining key milestones and deadlines.ConclusionThis project aims to significantly improve the performance, scalability, and deployment capabilities of the AI News Analysis web app. By rewriting the application code from scratch, developing a FastAPI API, and deploying the application on AWS Lambda, we aim to provide a robust solution that meets the immediate and future needs of our users.

title: Data Analyst required for historical Analysis of plant Data : Phase 1 of project
description: Current phase of our requirement is to start with only a historical analysis of the data captured from 6 of our plants across two different factory sites (3 individual plants in two factory location). Each of the 6 plants have very similar Scada data which is collected and stored every 15 minutes.A sample of the scada data available of one plant (Plant1) , for three months (from Jan 2020 to Mar 2020) in three separate files are attached as three separate spread sheets. These sheets are only a sample and to give you an idea of the data we are collecting. Eventually, data for each of the 6 plants in the 2 factory locations will be provided to you for the analysis, and we have such plant wise data for many years. Each of the 3 plants in the same factory location follow identical processes, and both of the factories have very similar process requirements too. Hence all 6 plants will have very similar processes and require identical analysis. The fourth file attached is an analysis done by our team, to give you an indication of the parameters which we find important. But please dont restrict your analysis only to the highlights in our analysis, please use all the data provided for your analysis and provide me with feedback purely from what the raw data is indicating.My requirement is for the data to be analyzed and feedback given from a statistical / data analytical perspective on how to increase our efficiency in our production operations. Attached with his posting are 4 excel files. Three of those files consists of sample data of one plant for 3 months (Jan to March of 2020). Looking at these files, I would like to maximize output from the two cells of:1. Increasing production per 15 minutes ( Column number BK of production every 15 minutes) and 2. Increasing kgs produced per unit of electricity in KwHr of electricity consumed (Column number DP).So I would like to understand how the other factors in the production data sheet influence these two columns in a positive or negative way.The deliverable is to provide a dashboard / model to show which parameters or in what conditions we maximise our production per 15 minutes, and our production per unit in KwHr of electricity consumed, that is both those columns (BK and DP) mentioned aboveI would also like a copy of all the code along with documentation. The contractor too needs to be available to demonstrate the results got based on the analysis. This is the first phase of the project. Later phases will be to add real time data to the model so that the model can prompt for action to be taken immediately to achieve highest production efficiency. Other plants from other factories will need to be added too. So the model will need to be structured and designed, and the code written, documented and delivered in such a way that other phases can be added on when requiredThe contractor should also be available for an online discussion before the project is confirmed and demonstrate his findings after too.Attached are four sample files:1. file name: DataLog report Plant1 jan 2020.xlsx has sample data for one plant (Plant 1) for the month of Jan 20202. File name: DataLog report Plant 1 Feb 2020.xlsx has sample data for the same plant (Plant 1) for the month of Feb 20203. File name: Datalog report Plant 1 Mar 2020.xlsx has sample data for Plant 1 for the month of Mar 2020The above three files are only a sample and to give you an idea for only one plant for 3 months. Eventually the project will require analysis for 6 plants over many years (close to a decade) All the the 6 plant files will be shared monthwise with you once the terms of the project are confirmed.4. File name: Plant 1 flow analysis report is a report included to indicate the parameters and columns we focus on in our analysis, to give you and idea on the columns to start with. But please dont restrict your analysis to these columns only, please see if patterns or correlations and causation's can be found with all the data provided.

title: Develop AI/Machine Learning Model to Critique Music
description: We're seeking an experienced AI/Machine Learning Developer to join our team in enhancing our online music platform. This platform empowers musicians to upload their tracks for evaluation by industry professionals, utilizing a 1-5 star rating system. Your primary responsibility will be to develop an AI/machine learning model capable of analyzing uploaded music and generating ratings on the 1-5 scale. Below, we outline the key steps involved in this exciting project:Step 1 - Platform Requirements Definition:Collaborate with our team to clearly define the platform's goals and requirements, establishing criteria for critiquing music on the 1-5 scale. Identify the musical features to be evaluated, such as melody, rhythm, and production quality, to guide the rating generation process.Step 2 - Data Collection:Lead the gathering of a diverse dataset of music tracks, each labeled with ratings on the 1-5 scale. Ensure the dataset encompasses various music genres and styles, enabling the AI model to provide meaningful critiques across the spectrum.Step 3 - Feature Extraction:Utilize advanced techniques to extract pertinent features from the music tracks. These features will serve as input for the AI model and may include tempo, key, chord progression, and spectral characteristics, among others.Step 4 - Model Selection:Identify or develop a suitable machine learning model capable of analyzing extracted features and generating accurate ratings on the 1-5 scale. title: Odds Plug In
description: Im looking for soemone who could create a WP plugin that sits on a website page so people can work out odds on a competition.So they would input - ticket price, number of tickets and this gives them the odds and total value like below -If the ticket price is £34.97 and there are 1999 tickets sold, and assuming the odds are still 2.00 (implying a 50% chance of winning), we'll calculate the chance of winning using the same method.First, let's calculate the total amount collected from selling tickets:Total amount collected = Price per ticket * Number of tickets= £34.97 * 1999≈ £69,899.03Now, let's calculate the potential payout for the winner. Since the odds are 2.00, for every unit bet (£34.97 in this case), the winner would receive £34.97 * 2 = £69.94.The chance of winning is the potential payout divided by the total amount collected:Chance of winning = Potential payout / Total amount collected= (£34.97 * 2) / (£34.97 * 1999)= 2 / 1999≈ 0.0010005To express this as a percentage, multiply by 100:Chance of winning ≈ 0.0010005 * 100≈ 0.10005%So, with the given odds, ticket price, and number of tickets sold, the chance of winning is approximately 0.10005%.

title: Data Analysis
description: Certainly! Data analysis is a process of inspecting, cleaning, transforming, and modeling data with the goal of discovering useful information, drawing conclusions, and supporting decision-making. Here are some key steps and concepts involved in data analysis:1. **Define Objectives:**- Clearly define the goals and objectives of your analysis. What do you want to achieve? What questions are you trying to answer?2. **Data Collection:**- Gather relevant data from various sources. This could be from databases, surveys, sensors, APIs, etc.3. **Data Cleaning:**- Preprocess and clean the data to handle missing values, outliers, and inconsistencies. This step is crucial to ensure the accuracy and reliability of your analysis.4. **Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA):**- Explore the data using descriptive statistics, visualizations, and summary tables to understand its structure, patterns, and relationships. This step helps in generating hypotheses and insights.5. **Data Transformation:**- Transform the data if needed, such as scaling, normalizing, encoding categorical variables, or creating new features.6. **Statistical Analysis:**- Apply statistical methods to test hypotheses, identify patterns, and make inferences about the population based on sample data.7. **Machine Learning:**- Implement machine learning algorithms for predictive modeling or classification tasks, depending on the nature of your analysis.8. **Data Visualization:**- Create visual representations of the data using charts, graphs, and dashboards to communicate insights effectively.9. **Interpretation and Conclusion:**- Draw conclusions from the analysis and interpret the results in the context of your objectives. Communicate findings in a clear and understandable manner.10. **Documentation:**- Document your analysis process, methodologies, and results. This is essential for reproducibility and for others to understand and validate your work.11. **Feedback and Iteration:**- Seek feedback from stakeholders and iterate on your analysis if needed. Continuous improvement is crucial in data analysis.Popular tools for data analysis include Python with libraries like Pandas, NumPy, and Matplotlib, R, and tools like SQL for database queries. Additionally, specialized tools such as Excel, Tableau, and Jupyter Notebooks are commonly used in the field.

The core functionality of this calculator should hinge on analyzing and integrating several key variables: the total project hours needed for completion, the productivity rate of the crew (expressed as a percentage reflecting the actual productive hours out of a standard workday), the size of the crew involved, and the flexibility in working days per week (ranging from a traditional 5-day workweek to extended options of 6 or even 4 days, adjusting for longer or shorter weeks). This tool must adeptly handle the calculation of required daily productive hours for the crew as a whole, taking into account the specified productivity rate, which can vary from 82% (where, for example, out of an 8-hour day, 6.56 hours are effectively productive) to a maximum of 94%. It should provide adjustable parameters for the analyst to simulate different scenarios, such as increasing the workday length to 9 hours or modifying the workweek, and calculate the impact of these adjustments on meeting the project deadline. Crucially, the calculator must offer insights into how changes in daily productivity affect the overall project timeline and suggest optimal working conditions to ensure project completion within the desired timeframe. By inputting different productivity rates, crew sizes, and working conditions, the tool should be able to forecast the total number of working days required to meet the project goal of, say, 1300 hours, and recommend adjustments to daily working hours or crew productivity rates necessary to achieve this target on time. This functionality will be instrumental in planning and decision-making processes, allowing for precise adjustments to work schedules, resource allocation, or project scope as needed to ensure timely and efficient project delivery. The end product should be a user-friendly, interactive calculator that enables quick scenario testing and provides clear, actionable output to guide project managers in optimizing their team's work schedule and productivity strategies for on-time project completion. title: Slack API Flask App
description: I have a program analyzing videos trends and sending alerts for the videos whose trends are increasing. title: Build Shopify plugin

The second component integrates directly into the checkout process of a merchant's Shopify store. It allows consumers who are checking out to use the resale value of their past purchases to pay for their current order. title: Shopify Website Developer Needed for numerous tasks and tweaks
description: Scope of the workWe need a developer to complete the following tasks:- Install Klaviyo for sign-up form functionality- Update footer to adapt form functionality- Install hydrogen-redirect-theme to handle *.myshopify.com redirects- Change fabrics page to be organised by fabric type, rather than colour- Make sure CTA buttons are yellow (fabrics page)- Check canonical URLs either do or do not contain trailing slashes based on how URL is being presentedWe estimate this is a half days work.We are available to work closely and get everything approved quickly.We have more complicated work that needs doing too so this would be a test run to build trust and hopefully a long standing relationship.Ideal developer experience - React, Typescript, Sanity, Remix (Shopify Hydrogen), Shopify, TailwindToolsShopify Hydrogen / RemixA headless stack built by Shopify on top of the Remix framework that exposes all of the Shopify API’s to our frontend application.Shopify OxygenUsed as the hosting for the Hydrogen app. This has been added as a Sales Channel and can be found in the Shopify Admin - Sales Channels - Hydrogen. Here is where you can manage the hosting configuration.SanityUsed for the CMS and deployed to Vercel.Sanity ConnectA Shopify app developed by the Sanity team that has been added to the Shopify Admin to sync data between Shopify and Sanity automatically. Products and collections are managed in Shopify and when synced to Sanity provide their data in the store object on their respective document.BoilerplateThe project was built on top of this repository https://github.com/sanity-io/hydrogen-sanity-demo from the Sanity team which provides a good clean example of how our frontend is constructed. This adopts many of Hydrogen's conventions and suggested third-party libraries. We haven’t strayed too far at all from the conventions defined here so this is a great resource.Tailwind CSSUsed predominantly to style the frontend.KLAVIYOKLAVIYO will be the CRM of choice and the frontend uses it for the newsletter signup form. There’s no custom form on the frontend connected to KLAVIYO.Source CodeThe code is stored and managed on Github in two separate repos (frontend, backend). The project takes a headless approach so the two are kept separate.The frontend is hosted on Shopify and the backend is hosted on Vercel.Local DevelopmentNothing of note to add here. Standard development practice to get the apps to run locally (check the package.json for commands available):FrontendTo get started, run npm install to install dependencies. Then run npm run dev to start the local server. To preview builds as you would on production, run npm run preview .BackendTo get started, run npm install to install dependencies. Then run npm run dev to start the local server.DeploymentOnce the Github repos are connected to Vercel and Shopify Oxygen then deployments happen automatically when code is pushed to git.

title: Research Assistant for Web Design Inspiration
description: I posted a job last year for a website designer / developer that I unfortunately didn't fill because realized I lacked the vision and direction needed to guide the individual I would hire.In other words, I didn't know what I wanted to build. I still quite don't.In a nutshell, I was missing both the high level structure / architecture (CMS, landing / other pages, navigation, content, UI etc...) -- but more importantly, I still hadn't quite defined the exact type of website and its core purpose.Taking a step back -- my background, 25 year career and domain expertise is primarily in finance / investing. For the last 15 years I have led and directed what is commonly referred to as a Single Family Office -- we allocate capital across a variety of asset classes in a similar way that and endowment or pension fund would (think of Calpers or the Yale Endowment). My work is to originate / source fund managers (aka investment sponsors) and also direct investments across asset classes. For every deal or investment we originate we conduct a initial screen / due diligence process before feeding it into our pipeline funnel which we then cull down to a select number of investment candidates that we research in depth and underwrite before deciding to invest or pass. Sorry if that sounds too technical / boring, just want to provide this info for context.Back to what I am looking to build and what I need help with.Ultimately I am looking to build a website that is a blend between a personal website and a portfolio website that can generate business leads for me as an independent professional (this will be used outside of my "day job"). I want to have a digitally native platform to showcase my experience and work. Importantly, in addition to showcasing past and ongoing projects I will need this platform to have communication functionality -- ideally allowing prospective clients or capital partners to engage with the content and register to become part of my "list" of followers (some sort of hybrid between a sub stack newsletter list and / or a registration that offers a subscription). It is common in my world for dealmakers to form what are called syndicates -- I want to build my own using this website as my main channel in building this group. The hook is showcasing past investments deals with good outcomes, combined with teasers of live deals that are available, and then reeling them in -- hook, line and sinker.I want this platform to narrate the story of how I made these investments, the deep dives into my process and thesis behind each. But here's the catch – I want it to be engaging, not just a static display of past projects -- so integrating something like sub stack or a format that resembles a portal that has more information behind a registration / verification of who the reader is (to capture their name / info and whether they are an accredited investor -- more on this later)So what do I need exactly? I need you to find examples of websites that hit the mark in finance or other sectors, blending professional showcase with personal narrative and interactive elements. I'm looking for someone who can dive into the digital world, identify sites that stand out for their design, structure, and ability to engage visitors, and then bring those insights back to me. I'm particularly interested in how these sites manage to convert their audience with calls to action – whether it's subscribing to a service or jumping on investment opportunities.This task isn't just about compiling a list. It's about understanding what makes these sites work and how those elements can be woven into the fabric of what I'm trying to build. It's about envisioning a platform where sharing my story & experience, the depth of my investment analysis and quality of my work, and teasing with opportunities I see ahead & can be shared in a way that invites collaboration, partnership, and growth.If you have a background in web development and are able to delve deep to dissect web design trends -- and can kind of enter my world of finance / investing to understand some of the nuance -- I think you could be a great fit for this project. I'm looking for someone who can not only identify inspiring websites but also articulate why they're effective and how we might draw from them to create something unique.This project is more than just a digital business card or portfolio for me; it's about building a bridge to future clients / partnerships + opportunities.

title: Full Stack Developer needed for custom website that allows end user to design custom stickers.
description: Designing and implementing a system to allow consumers to create and upload images for label manufacturing involves several components, including front-end development, back-end development, and integration with a database (Excel typically). Below is a simplified outline using a web-based technology stack. Keep in mind that this is a general guide, and the specific requirements may vary based on our needs. The product can be viewed on Facebook at https://www.facebook.com/helpsticker/Front-end (Client-Side):Web Interface:Create a user-friendly web interface where consumers can design their labels.Use HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for building the interface.Consider using a front-end framework like React, Angular, or Vue.js for a more structured approach.Image Editing:Integrate an image editing library or tool to allow users to customize their labels. You could use libraries like Fabric.js, Konva.js, or an HTML5 canvas for this purpose.Image Upload:Implement a feature to allow users to upload their designed images.Utilize HTML "input type="file"" or more advanced libraries like Dropzone.js for file uploads.Back-end (Server-Side):Server-Side Language:Choose a server-side language such as Node.js, Python (Django or Flask), Ruby on Rails, or Java.Image Handling:Implement server-side code to handle and process the uploaded images. Resize or format the images as needed for printing.Storage:Set up a storage solution (e.g., Amazon S3, Google Cloud Storage) to store the uploaded images securely.Database:Use a database (e.g., MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB) to store information about the uploaded images, associated orders, and user details.Authentication and Authorization:Implement user authentication and authorization to secure the application.Integration:APIs:Create APIs to facilitate communication between the front-end and back-end. Use RESTful or GraphQL APIs for data exchange.Communication with Label Manufacturing Companies:Establish a system for communicating with the label manufacturing companies. This could involve integrating with their APIs or setting up a data transfer process.Order Processing:Develop a mechanism to process user orders, including sending the design specifications and image files to the label manufacturing companies.Security:SSL/TLS:Implement SSL/TLS for secure data transfer between the client and server.Data Validation and Sanitization:Validate and sanitize user inputs to prevent security vulnerabilities such as SQL injection or cross-site scripting (XSS).User Authentication and Authorization:Ensure that only authenticated and authorized users can access and modify their data.Remember, the specific implementation details and technologies may vary based on your project requirements and the label manufacturing companies' systems. It's crucial to consider factors such as security, scalability, and the manufacturing companies' technical capabilities during the development process. Additionally, consulting with the label manufacturing companies regarding their preferred integration methods is recommended.

title: Merge csv files into single excel
description: ========================================Project Title: PowerShell Script for Importing CSV Files into Excel SheetsObjective: The objective of this project is to develop a PowerShell script that imports CSV files into Excel sheets based on specified parameters. The script should be able to handle numbered subdirectories, locate template Excel files, read corresponding map files, and print all parameters before execution.========================================Scope:The script will be developed using PowerShell scripting language.The script will accept a directory path as a parameter, representing the base directory where the operation will be performed.The script will loop through all numbered subdirectories (1,2,3,...) within the base directory.Within each subdirectory, the script will locate all CSV files and corresponding map files.Map files will be in the format of ".csv file name.map" and will contain two columns: XLS_SHEET and XLS_LINE.The script will locate the template Excel file (template.xlsx or template.xls) in a template directory, which is a subdirectory of the base directory.If multiple template files are found, the script will prioritize template.xlsx over template.xls.The script will copy the selected template file into each numbered subdirectory for subsequent operations.CSV files will be imported into different Excel sheets within the template file.Excel sheet names will be defined by the XLS_SHEET column in the corresponding map file.CSV files will be imported starting from the line specified in the XLS_LINE column of the map file.Before executing the import operation, the script will print all parameters for validation and debugging purposes.========================================Out of Scope:The script will not handle exceptions such as missing files or incorrect file formats beyond basic validation.The script will not perform any data validation or transformation on the imported data.The script will not modify the original CSV files or template Excel files.========================================Assumptions:The base directory provided as a parameter will contain numbered subdirectories.Each numbered subdirectory will contain CSV files and corresponding map files.Template Excel files will be located in a subdirectory named "template" within the base directory.CSV files and map files will have consistent naming conventions and formats.The script will be executed in a PowerShell environment where the ImportExcel module is installed and available.========================================Deliverables:PowerShell script file (import-csv-to-excel.ps1) implementing the specified functionality.Documentation including a scope document, usage instructions, and any additional notes deemed necessary.========================================Dependencies:PowerShell environment with access to the ImportExcel module.Proper permissions to read and write files within the specified directories.========================================Attachment are examples of 2 files

title: Modifying & Updating a custom WordPress Plugin to PHP 8 Compatibility
description: Hi,We had a custom WordPress Plugin created before and it's worked solidly so far but we need to make some changes to it.1. The plugin needs to be updated to be PHP 8 compatible.2. The plugin has a shortcode that works correctly, but has an issue with caching causing it to show in the page when it shouldn't.The way it was originally designed was that the PHP generated HTML from the shortcode is ONLY visible when javascript is disabled with no script tags but this isn't happening when the page gets cached resulting it showing on devices where javascript is enabled.The issue is to do with LiteSpeed Cache / Other Caching plugins. We do not want to disable caching on this page. The attempted fix we tried to implement before was using LiteSpeeds Vary Cache. but that never worked.The whole reason we need this is to provide some content for search engine crawlers to be able to get some content.3. The plugin has a function to ping google asking them to crawl the sitemap, it was setup incorrectly but also now Google has discontinued this feature so we are wanting to remove this from the code, but make sure the sitemap data we're providing to WordPress contains the correct LastMod element so crawlers know when it was last modified.4. We need a change so if an item is retrieved in an API response and then later is no longer found in an API response that it doesn't delete the temporary wordpress post but simply hides/unpublishes it.This is because we want a setting added for "Unpublish Expired Items" which should be enabled by default. If enabled then for crawlers/humans the pages would all act identically to they do now however if it's disabled then expired items wouldn't be deleted but instead updated to have a "This item is expired, please visit xxxxx"5. We need simple a user interface created that would list all of the currently retrieved items from the API. It should show the date & time of when they were first retrieved and have a button on the right hand side to "Unpublish" and "Republish" them allowing more control of what goes into the sitemap. If a user changes one of these it would override the "Unpublish Expired Items" feature mentioned in #46. The plugin also needs a button to manually trigger the plugin to check the API for new items.

title: Simple Tableau Data Analysis
description: ACME, home of the ACME Kleen Earth Office Shears, is a chain of stores with locations around the world. The dataset contained here includes orders, returns, and customer information.We will use these data for our Data Analytics exercises. The data (Excel) can be found in the attachment. You can register in Tableau for free. Register today as sometimes verification process might take longer than what is expected.Work instructionsCustomer Categorization: The concept began in B2B marketing long ago, and, like Relationship Marketing, has also been adopted by B2C marketing. This idea is simple and closely related to inventory management control. Customers come in three types, A, B and C.‘A’ customers are your most profitable. According to the Pareto Principle, 20% of your customers account for 80% of your profit. These customers deserve your attention and priority. Keep them coming back.‘C’ customers may not be profitable at all or account for very little profit. They’re probably not worth the effort put into them and can be dropped or dissuaded from returning. At the very least, ignore them.‘B’ customers are somewhere in the middle. The aggregate of their sales is large but their profitability is nowhere near ‘A’ customers. Can they be turned into ‘A’ customers? Are they worth that effort?If you’re interested in learning more about customer categorization and profit try this (optional) Harvard Business Review article:This job entails, you guessed it, categorizing Acme’s customers. Identify A, B, and C customers in your assigned Segment (each customer will belong to one of three “buckets”).Analyze the Corporate segment.Build a Story (in Tableau) to show the 3 groups and visually show their profitability (hint: this requires more than just a list of names, but make sure the names are there). (Hint: Tableau wants to cut off the list and you're going to have to do some manipulation to get the top 20 to show properly.) (Note: It's a lot more interesting if you use the bottom of the C customer list rather than the top but it's your choice as to which to show.)Then, go at least one level deeper into the analysis. (This entails figuring out what kind of analysis would be useful as well as performing it.)Your deliverableYou must complete the assignment in Tableau. Then, you will submit a Word document that includes:The Story (create in Tableau; paste into Word) Include evidence that you created the categories; show your customer names (top 20 in each category).What additional analysis did you do? At least two additional analysis you need to conduct.What marketing tactics should be used for each group? (Be specific to your segment.)What would be your next steps in analysis to dig even deeper? only describe what you would do next. No need for actually doing it in Tableau.To help you familiarize yourself with this software, you can watch the following video tutorials:https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hr5IE0qYkRshttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jj6-0cvcNEAhttps://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fO7g0pnWaRAPlease note: some of these links are two-hour long videos.

description: We are looking for a business intelligence analyst that can support our team remotely and expand the current BI landscape that is already in place.To select the right candidate we have created a technical challenge designed to assess your skills in Business Intelligence, specifically focusing on analyzing application usage data. This challenge aims to simulate a real-world scenario where you'll be tasked with extracting insights from application usage data to inform business decisions. You will be using Google BigQuery for data analysis and Google Looker Studio for data visualization. This is an opportunity to showcase your ability to work with complex datasets, your analytical thinking, and your proficiency in creating compelling data visualizations.Objective:Your goal is to analyze a dataset representing user interactions with a web application, focusing on user engagement, feature usage, and retention. Using the Google Analytics Sample Dataset for BigQuery, you will derive insights into how users interact with the application, identify patterns, and visualize these insights in a dashboard using Google Looker Studio.Step 1: Data Analysis in BigQuery:- **Dataset:** `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample`- **Tasks:**1. **Calculate Engagement Metrics:** Determine Daily Active Users (DAU) and Monthly Active Users (MAU).2. **Feature Analysis:** Identify the most and least used features by querying event data.3. **Demographic and Cohort Analysis:** Join user demographic information with session data to analyze usage patterns. Perform a cohort analysis based on user signup date to study retention.4. **Advanced Analysis:** Incorporate session duration and time-of-day analysis to explore when users are most active.Step 2: Visualization in Google Looker Studio:- **Objective:** Create a dashboard in Google Looker Studio that clearly presents your findings from BigQuery, including:1. **Engagement Trends:** Visualize DAU and MAU over time.2. **Feature Popularity:** Chart showing feature usage frequency.3. **User Demographics:** Insights into user engagement segmented by demographics.4. **Cohort Retention:** Visualization of retention rates for different cohorts.5. **Interactive Elements:** Ensure the dashboard includes filters or interactive elements for a deeper data dive.Evaluation Criteria:- **SQL Proficiency:** Complexity and efficiency of SQL queries.- **Analytical Skills:** Ability to extract meaningful insights from complex data.- **Visualization Expertise:** Clarity and effectiveness of the dashboard in communicating insights.- **Data Storytelling:** Competence in narrating a data-driven story that supports business decisions.Dataset Access:- Access the dataset directly in Google Cloud's BigQuery under `bigquery-public-data.google_analytics_sample`.- Use standard SQL in the BigQuery console for analysis.Submission Requirements:- Provide SQL queries used for the analysis.- Share a link to the Looker Studio dashboard.- Include a brief report summarizing key insights and potential recommendations for improving user engagement and retention.Timeframe:- The challenge is designed to be completed within 1-2 hours.- We will not be able to review the results until Wed. 28th FebThis technical challenge is an opportunity to demonstrate your ability to work with real-world data, using advanced SQL queries and data visualization tools to drive business intelligence insights. Good luck!

title: Website need hosting changing from GoDaddy to site ground
description: To effectively move your landing page from GoDaddy to SiteGround, follow these steps:Backup Your Landing Page: Before initiating any transfer, ensure you have a backup of your landing page files and database to prevent data loss.Access Your GoDaddy Account: Log in to your GoDaddy account and locate your domain settings. You'll need to update the domain's DNS settings to point to SiteGround's servers.Retrieve SiteGround Nameservers: Log in to your SiteGround account and navigate to the domain management section. Take note of the nameservers provided by SiteGround.Update Nameservers on GoDaddy: In your GoDaddy account, find the domain associated with your landing page and update the nameservers to the ones provided by SiteGround. This change may take some time to propagate across the internet.Transfer Landing Page Files: Using FTP or File Manager in cPanel, transfer your landing page files from your GoDaddy hosting to your SiteGround hosting account. Make sure to replicate the directory structure and permissions as needed.Import Database (If Applicable): If your landing page relies on a database, export the database from GoDaddy's hosting control panel and import it into your SiteGround hosting account. Update any configuration files to point to the new database location if necessary.Update Configuration Settings: Update any configuration settings within your landing page files to reflect the new hosting environment, including database connection details and file paths.Test Your Landing Page: Once the migration is complete, thoroughly test your landing page on SiteGround to ensure all functionalities are working correctly.Update DNS Records (Optional): If your landing page utilizes specific DNS records (e.g., MX records for email), make sure to update them in your SiteGround account accordingly.Monitor for Propagation: Keep an eye on your domain's DNS propagation status to ensure the changes have fully taken effect. This process can take up to 24-48 hours to complete.Cancel GoDaddy Hosting (If Desired): Once you've confirmed that your landing page is successfully hosted on SiteGround and all necessary data has been migrated, you can cancel your hosting subscription with GoDaddy if you no longer wish to use their services.

description: Looking for someone who can write a script to scrape all 3000+ US Counties on Redfin on a weekly basis to see active listings vs sold listings (1 month, 3 month, 6 month, 1 year time frames)I use Redfin extensively. The process I use to analyze demand in a market is the following:I choose a county in a state, say cullman county, AL. I then filter for listings 5 acres or more. I then see how many listings are currently available for sale and take note of that number - can call it (Total Active Sales Listing). Then I filter the view to show "Last 1 Month Sold", taking note of that (1 month Sold). Then I filter to "Last 3 Months Sold" (3 months sold). Then filter to "Last 6 Months Sold" (6 months sold). Then "Last 1 Year Sold" ( 1 year sold). I then take each value and divide by the (Total Active Sales) to find the Sell Through Rate for each time period so for instance - the 1 Month Sell Through Rate = (1 month Sold) / (Total Active Sales Listings). I would like to be able to pull this rate each week for all 3000+ counties in the US so that I can gauge demand.

title: Backend for IoT devices with simple web portal
description: We require a back-end implementation for a simple IoT device that will be uploading JSON data for position and some other metadata. We would like to use access keys for authentication, where each device is assigned an ID and a key, securely stored in the device and transmitted as part of the JSON string.The connections will always be via cellular and HTTPS is preferred. We would prefer not to have to use X509 and client certificates. Approximately one packet per hour will be transmitted from each device, and there will be initially only a few devices, expanding eventually to around 1000 maximum.The choice of back-end is up to the developer, we have an Azure instance already but are not averse to creating a subscription with another provider if it will save on costs.The data shall be stored in a database, again it is down to the developer to recommend specific implementation however we are looking for a cost effective solution and performance is not paramount.The web portal shall initially be a very simple maintenance and commissioning page that can be used by the manufacturer of the IoT devices to load them with the keys.As devices are deployed into the field, a desirable function of the website would be to have a login page where registered users (users will be created by the system administrator using the administrative page used to commission devices) can log in using a pre-created set of credentials and view some details pertaining to a single device, presented in a form to be determined but could include a photo of the device and some other details, including the latest data sent from the device itsself. Some of the data is geolocation, and a desirable goal would be to have a map that can show the last uploaded location.We would like to define the API and the server used (and therefore the endpoint addresses and key format) fairly quickly as the first prototype devices are going to be in the hands of testers in the next couple of weeks. We do not need the website operational in this time, but we need to finalise the device firmware for the first device.

title: Build a Shopify public app using Shopify Polaris, Remix and Prisma Database
description: Project Overview:We are seeking a skilled developer to create a Shopify Public App that automates the addition of deposit fees to products in a Shopify store, with a strong emphasis on localization. This app will enable store owners to assign specific deposit amounts to individual products, ensuring that when these products are added to the cart, the corresponding deposit fee is automatically included. This system aims to streamline the process of managing deposits for products such as beverage containers, where a deposit fee is required. The app must be designed to be easily translatable into all languages to accommodate store owners and customers worldwide.Key Features:Deposit Management Settings Page:A user-friendly interface for store owners to create and manage deposit amounts.Ability to define deposit names and corresponding deposit amounts.The interface should be designed to support localization, allowing translations into multiple languages for global usability.Product Selection for Deposits:A dedicated page for selecting products to assign specific deposit amounts.Capability to link different deposit amounts to different products, e.g., $0.10 for beer bottles, $0.30 for wine bottles, etc.Support for localization in product selection and deposit assignment interfaces.Cart Update Logic:Automatic update of the shopping cart to include the deposit fee when a product with an assigned deposit is added.The deposit quantity should match the quantity of the associated product added to the cart (e.g., adding three beer bottles adds three $0.10 deposits).Upon removal of a product from the cart, the corresponding deposit line item should also be removed.Cart updates and messages should be translatable, supporting a seamless shopping experience in multiple languages.Technical Requirements:Framework: The app should be built using Remix, a modern React framework, to ensure a robust and scalable application architecture.UI Components: Utilize Shopify Polaris for designing the user interface, ensuring a consistent look and feel with Shopify's native UI. The design should be adaptable for localization.Data Management: Implement Prisma as the ORM for efficient database management, handling the storage and retrieval of deposit settings and product-deposit associations, with support for storing localized content.Shopify Integration: The application must comply with Shopify's API requirements for public apps, ensuring seamless integration and operation within the Shopify ecosystem.Localization Support: The app should include a framework or library to support internationalization (i18n) and localization (l10n), enabling easy translation of UI texts, messages, and data inputs into various languages.Responsiveness and Compatibility: The app should be fully responsive and compatible with a range of devices and screen sizes, ensuring a seamless user experience across desktop and mobile.Ideal Candidate:Proficiency in React and familiarity with the Remix framework.Experience in developing Shopify apps and working with Shopify's Polaris UI library.Strong background in database management, especially with Prisma ORM.Demonstrated ability to integrate third-party apps with Shopify stores.Expertise in implementing localization and internationalization in web applications.Attention to detail and a commitment to creating a user-friendly and globally accessible interface.Ability to write clean, maintainable, and efficient code.Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently.Project Outcome:The successful development of this Shopify Public App will significantly simplify the process of managing deposits for products sold in Shopify stores, with the added benefit of full localization support. It will automate the addition and removal of deposit fees in the shopping cart, ensuring accuracy and efficiency in handling these transactions, while providing a valuable tool for Shopify store owners globally, enhancing their ability to manage product deposits effectively and improving the shopping experience for their customers across different languages.How to Apply:Interested candidates should submit a portfolio of relevant work, including any previous Shopify apps or projects that demonstrate experience with React, Remix, Shopify Polaris, Prisma, and especially localization or internationalization implementations. Please include a brief overview of your approach to the project, highlighting how you plan to tackle the localization requirements, along with any initial thoughts or questions you may have.

title: Proposal Needed Scale existing WebApp PHP Laravel Mysql to Run on AWS Elastic beanstalk with RDS DB
description: We are seeking a comprehensive proposal encompassing the entire process from A to Z, including methodology, in a PDF/Word Document format for our existing PHP Laravel Web application. The application currently runs on an Ubuntu 22.04 OS, utilizing PHP FPM 8.1, Nginx, and MySQLDB.Presently, our application operates within a single-server environment. However, we have encountered instances where the server experiences significant load, resulting in decreased application performance. As a solution, we intend to migrate the application to Amazon Web Services (AWS), specifically deploying it on Elastic Beanstalk with MySQL RDS.Our objective is to maintain a single instance running at all times, with additional instances provisioned automatically when server utilization surpasses 80%. Once utilization falls below 80%, we aim to revert to a single running instance. Currently, we utilize a t2.medium instance with a Public IP. Additionally, our domain is hosted on GoDaddy, and our code repository is managed through Git.Our primary goals for this migration are cost-efficiency and scalability. While we are considering Elastic Beanstalk, we are open to alternative solutions if they offer a more cost-effective approach. For instance, Docker image deployment with Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (EKS) could be a viable alternative.We are specifically seeking proposals from individuals or teams with prior experience in similar projects. Thank you.
